items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Jammu & Kashmir High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Justice Bhati is currently a judge of the Rajasthan High Court. The decision to recommend his name for Chief Justice was taken by the collegium in a meeting held on August 31. If the Centre confirms the collegium's recommendation, Justice Bhati will take over as Chief Justice from Justice Sanjeev Kumar who has been serving as Acting Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since June 2, 2026. Justice Bhati was a lawyer practicing across several areas of law for nearly 25 before he was elevated to the Bench of the Rajasthan High Court on November 16, 2016. As a lawyer, he served as a Additional Advocate General for the State and was elected as President of the High Court Lawyers Association at different points Justice Bhati's wife, Justice Nupur Bhati was also elevated as a judge of the Rajasthan High Court in 2023.

items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice AY Kogje as Chief Justice of Madhya Pradesh High Court
items.summary: Justice Alpesh Yeshvant Kogje from Gujarat High Court has been recommended for appointment as the Chief Justice of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The recommendation was made by the Supreme Court Collegium in its meeting held on August 31. Justice Kogje is presently serving as a judge of the Gujarat High Court. Justice Kogje completed his B.Sc. in Chemistry in 1990 and earned his law degree from the Faculty of Law at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda in 1993. He joined the Bar in 1993, building a robust practice in civil and criminal matters before the High Court. Throughout his career as counsel, he held several significant roles, including Additional Public Prosecutor from 2002 to 2007, Standing Counsel for the Central Excise and Customs Department, and Special Public Prosecutor for the Special Investigation Team (SIT), where he notably handled a large volume of important cases arising from the 2002 Godhra riots. He was elevated as an Additional Judge of the Gujarat High Court in April 2016. He was subsequently appointed as a permanent Judge of the Gujarat High Court in March 2018. The Madhya Pradesh High Court is presently functioning with 38 judges while its sanctioned strength is 53. [Read Collegium Statement]
